transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’ve been feeling really restless, like I can’t settle in my own body. It’s especially noticeable when I’m supposed to sit quietly and do things like paperwork or talk through household plans with someone. I just feel keyed up and uncomfortable.
Have you started or changed any medications recently, especially antipsychotics or anti-nausea drugs, before these restless feelings began?
I don’t think so. I can’t think of any medication change that happened right before this started.

When you feel this restlessness, do you notice a strong urge to move—like pacing, shifting your weight, or rocking your legs—that actually feels better once you move, or is it more a sense of worry and mental tension regardless of movement?

It’s more like I just can’t settle in my body, especially when I’m supposed to sit still and deal with paperwork or talk through household plans. I feel restless and uncomfortable, like I need to do something, but the main thing is that sitting quietly feels really hard.

Besides the restlessness, have you noticed any other physical changes lately—like your heart racing, hand tremors, unexplained weight loss, excessive sweating, or feeling unusually hot or intolerant to warm temperatures?
No, not really. I haven’t noticed things like my heart racing or shaking or sweating more than usual. I don’t think I’ve had any unexplained weight loss or feeling unusually hot either.
Do you also find yourself worrying excessively about different things—like your health, family, or work—along with this restlessness, or is it mainly the physical urge to move that's bothering you?

It’s mainly that I can’t settle in my body. I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there worrying about a bunch of different things. It’s more when I’m supposed to sit quietly and do paperwork or talk through household plans, I just feel like I need to get up or do something.

Have you ever taken, or are you currently taking, any antipsychotic medications (like risperidone or haloperidol) or anti-nausea drugs (like metoclopramide or prochlorperazine), even if it was months ago?
I don’t think so. I’m not currently taking anything like that, and I don’t remember being prescribed those kinds of medications before.
Does this restless feeling tend to get worse in the evening or at night, particularly when you're lying down to rest or trying to fall asleep?

Not especially at night, no. It’s more when I’m expected to sit still and focus on things like paperwork or talking through household plans. That’s when I feel like I can’t really settle in my own body and I just want to get up or do something.
Has this kind of restlessness with sitting still and focusing on tasks been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a new problem that started more recently in your life?

It’s definitely not new. Looking back, it was already there when I was in elementary school. I was the kid with the messy desk and forgotten permission slips, and teachers would send notes home saying I talked out of turn or couldn’t seem to stay in my seat.
Do you currently find yourself easily distracted, losing track of details, or forgetting things in daily life, work, or conversations?

Yes, definitely. I get pulled off track really easily. Like if I’m trying to do something at the kitchen table, my phone buzzes, or I hear a car outside, or even just a thought about what to make for dinner pops up, and suddenly I’ve completely stopped what I was doing. Sometimes I don’t even notice right away that I’ve drifted off.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out answers before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Yes, I do. I really try to be respectful, but I catch myself jumping in before the other person is done. With my husband especially, I’ll interrupt or finish what I think he’s about to say, and it’s like the response is out of my mouth before I’ve made myself wait.
